currency_note: Wise switched reporting currency from GBP to USD starting FY2026 and moved primary listing to Nasdaq (WSE) in May 2026, retaining a secondary LSE listing (WISE). This entire DCF is modeled in USD millions (except per-share figures). WISE.L pence price is derived from the WSE USD price via spot GBPUSD for display purposes only.

inputs.net_debt_rationale: Wise carries $334.7m corporate borrowings (FY2026) but own (non-customer) cash comfortably exceeds this -- balance-sheet cash includes safeguarded customer funds which are not available to equity holders, so the full cash line is excluded. FY2023 disclosed own cash was ~£671m and the business has been strongly FCF-generative every year since (FY2024 $487.2m, FY2025 $535.8m, FY2026 $532.8m FCF), so net debt is treated conservatively as approximately zero rather than a precise (and likely negative/net-cash) figure that isn't cleanly disclosed in the metrics extract.

growth_analysis.rationale: Equity CAGR is not used as the primary driver: Wise now runs active share buybacks (new $500m+ program announced with FY2026 results), which mechanically distorts book-value growth and makes equity CAGR an unreliable proxy for business growth. EPS CAGR (55-83%) is also excluded as a primary driver -- it is inflated by margin expansion off a small FY2022 base and is not representative of a maturing, decelerating growth profile. FCF has flat-lined over 2 years (4.6% 2yr CAGR) purely because FY2026 was a deliberate heavy-investment year (operating income fell from $728.2m to $590.7m on step-ups in tech/marketing/compliance spend) -- extrapolating flat FCF would understate the business. Net revenue growth (trailing 34.8% 4yr CAGR, decelerating to 18-19% in FY25/26, with management guiding FY27 to the middle of a 15-20% medium-term range) is used as the primary top-line driver, with FCF modeled as a normalized margin (~19-23% depending on scenario) on that growing revenue base rather than extrapolated in absolute dollars.
growth_analysis.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 4yr CAGR (83.0%) diverges materially (>30%) from revenue 4yr CAGR (34.8%), reflecting operating leverage off a near-breakeven FY2022 base; this is expected for a scaling fintech and is why net revenue (not EPS or equity) was selected as the DCF growth driver. FCF 2yr CAGR (4.6%) also diverges sharply from revenue growth due to the deliberate FY2026 reinvestment year -- FCF margin is normalized in projections rather than the trailing 2yr FCF growth rate being extrapolated. Q1 FY2027 net revenue growth accelerated to +25% YoY ($714.0m), running ahead of management's FY2027 full-year guidance (middle of 15-20% range), reinforcing that the base-case deceleration path (16.5% Y1 to 10.0% Y5) is, if anything, conservative relative to current momentum.

entry_price.methodology: Entry price = (PV of Yr1-5 FCF discounted at 15% hurdle + PV of Year-5 Gordon terminal value [computed with WACC, discounted at 15%] - net debt) / shares. This replaces a prior broken methodology that discounted only the terminal value per share at 15%, ignoring interim FCF and the net-cash position, which understated the entry price by roughly 40%.

sensitivity.note: Matrix is base-case intrinsic value per share (USD) across WACC (rows) and terminal growth (columns); base-case growth path and FCF margin (21%) held constant. Terminal growth range is centered on the base-case 2.8% assumption (+/-1pp).

sanity_check.method: Compared base/bull/bear DCF intrinsic values (and implied forward multiples) against Wise's own historical trading multiples (FY-end LSE price converted to USD via month-end GBPUSD, vs USD diluted EPS and net revenue) to check the DCF isn't producing an implausible re-rating.

FY2022.note: excluded as hypergrowth-era outlier (near-breakeven EPS base)

trip_conditions_checked.threshold: 24.5x x 2 = 49.0x; base implied ~23x and bull implied ~33x are both well below this
trip_conditions_checked.detail: Base case upside is roughly -9.5% (below current price), not >100%, so this condition is not triggered
trip_conditions_checked.exit_multiple_detail: Current trailing EV/FCF is 23.9x. Base implied exit multiple is 14.3x and bull is 15.8x -- both well below current, meaning the DCF assumes de-rating (normalization), not multiple expansion.

sanity_check.result: PASS. Base-case implied P/E sits below the FY24-26 ex-outlier historical average (24.5x) and well below the current trailing multiple (25.6x), i.e. the DCF is not assuming any multiple expansion -- if anything a de-rating from today's trailing multiple, consistent with normalizing FCF margins off the FY2026 heavy-investment year and rate-cut headwinds to net interest income. Bull case implies a return toward the growth-stock premium multiples that analysts' price targets suggest (JPMorgan $17.30, BofA $16.40, Jefferies $16.60 PT all sit above the base case and near/above the bull case). Bear case is a plausible mature-payments-company de-rating. No fixes required.

valuation_philosophy: Wise is modeled as a decelerating high-growth fintech: net revenue growth (not equity or EPS CAGR) is the primary top-line driver because (a) equity CAGR is distorted by the new $500m+ buyback program, and (b) trailing FCF growth is artificially flat due to a single deliberate FY2026 reinvestment year, not a change in the underlying earnings power of the business. FCF is instead projected as a normalized margin on net revenue (19-23% across scenarios, below the FY2024 peak of 27.4% but roughly in line with or above FY2026's 21.3%), reflecting management's own guidance that FY2026 was a peak-investment year and that income-before-tax margin should sit near the top of a 20-25% medium-term range in FY2027 even as reinvestment continues. Given ~24% of FY2026 net revenue is net interest income on customer balances, all scenarios explicitly build in take-rate compression and a global rate-cutting cycle as the key structural headwinds; net debt is treated as approximately zero given corporate borrowings ($334.7m) are comfortably covered by non-customer cash and the business self-funds via strong recurring FCF generation. Both the sensitivity table and the historical multiple sanity check confirm the base case does not require multiple expansion to be reasonable -- it is close to (slightly below) Wise's own FY2024-26 trading range, with bull/bear cases bracketing the current Wall Street price-target dispersion ($16.10-$17.30) and a plausible mature-payments de-rating, respectively. The entry price methodology was corrected in this refresh: it now properly incorporates PV of interim FCF (2026-2031) plus the discounted terminal value at a 15% hurdle rate, net of the (approximately zero) net debt position, rather than discounting only the terminal per-share value -- the prior approach understated the true 15%-IRR entry point by roughly 40%.
assumptions: Net revenue is the primary DCF growth driver (not equity CAGR, which is distorted by active buybacks; not FCF CAGR, which is flat only due to a deliberate FY2026 investment year)

Base case: net revenue growth decelerating from 16.5% to 10.0% over 5 years, roughly tracking the middle of management's 15-20% medium-term guidance range and decelerating further into the terminal period -- conservative relative to the +25% YoY Q1 FY27 print

Bull case: net revenue growth 21.0% decelerating to 14.0%, consistent with sustained Wise Platform scaling, continued instant-payment rail expansion, and durable card/account revenue growth (+38% YoY in Q1 FY27)

Bear case: net revenue growth 11.0% decelerating to 6.0%, reflecting take-rate compression outpacing volume growth, a deeper global rate-cutting cycle hitting net interest income, and early stablecoin-rail share loss

FCF margin normalized at 21% (base), 23% (bull), 19% (bear) of net revenue -- below FY2024's 27.4% peak but consistent with FY2026's 21.3% actual and management's guided income-before-tax margin (top of 20-25% range) net of reinvestment and tax/working-capital drag

WACC: 10.0% base, 9.5% bull, 10.5% bear -- reflects large-cap, profitable, net-cash fintech profile offset by intensifying competition (Revolut, Remitly, stablecoin rails) and governance concentration (CEO holds ~50% voting control via Class B shares on ~18% economic interest)
Terminal growth: 2.8% base, 3.0% bull, 2.5% bear, in line with long-run nominal GDP/inflation expectations for a global payments infrastructure business

Net debt treated as approximately zero: $334.7m gross corporate borrowings offset by non-customer-fund own cash that has historically comfortably exceeded borrowings (FY2023 own cash ~£671m) plus strong ongoing FCF generation ($532.8m in FY2026)

Shares outstanding: 1,029.7m diluted (FY2026), before any impact of the newly announced $500m+ buyback program (which would be modestly accretive to per-share intrinsic value if executed, not modeled explicitly here)

Entry price (corrected methodology, effective this refresh): computed as PV of Year 1-5 base-case FCF discounted at a 15% hurdle rate, plus the Year-5 Gordon terminal value (computed using WACC, as it represents the fair price a future buyer would pay) discounted back at 15%, less net debt, divided by shares outstanding -- properly capturing that a buyer today also collects five years of substantial interim free cash flow, not just the exit value
